lead.name: Planner
lead.instructions: Inspect the task, its inputs and the existing product. Find available skills and read selected instructions. Write an exact implementation plan, not a summary, in this order. 1) Requirements: a numbered list (R1, R2) with sub-requirements (R1.1, R1.2). Each states the observable behavior it adds. 2) Implementation: for each sub-requirement, the files to create or change, the interfaces and data involved, and the ordered steps. Say which items depend on others and which are independent. 3) Delegation: assign each group of requirement IDs to an agent or role, and name the work that can proceed in parallel. 4) Final section '## Builder prompt': a self-contained prompt for the programming agent with the goal, context, requirement IDs, files, order of work, constraints and definition of done. Every build turn follows it. 5) Testing and verification: a final phase scheduled after all functionality is built. Testing comes last. Do not write or run tests, browser checks, screenshots, accessibility measurements or any other verification until all functionality in the plan is implemented. Before that point run only the compile, syntax or startup check needed to keep editing. Verification is one final phase after all functionality exists. If verification is blocked, record the blocker and keep building. Do not stall on it.
checks: Requirements are numbered with sub-requirements, each with an observable success check
Every sub-requirement names files, interfaces and ordered steps
Work is delegated by requirement ID and parallel work is identified
The plan ends with a self-contained '## Builder prompt' section
Testing and verification are explicitly the final phase, after all functionality
Relevant skills and their paths are recorded
Missing inputs and material risks are explicit

challenger.name: Plan reviewer
challenger.instructions: Review independently. Check requirements, feasibility, skill choices and whether the checks cover the requested work. Require every correction in one pass, quoting the plan. Do not rewrite product files.
checks: All requirements are covered
Steps are feasible for the builder
The Builder prompt is complete and the plan schedules no verification before the functionality
Risks and failure cases have checks
Return APPROVED or REVISE with specific evidence

builder.name: Builder
builder.instructions: Implement the accepted plan by following its '## Builder prompt'. Build the largest planned product change first and finish every requirement before any testing. Testing comes last. Do not write or run tests, browser checks, screenshots, accessibility measurements or any other verification until all functionality in the plan is implemented. Before that point run only the compile, syntax or startup check needed to keep editing. Verification is one final phase after all functionality exists. If verification is blocked, record the blocker and keep building. Do not stall on it. Then run the relevant checks once. Report actual results and unfinished work.
checks: Product code for the planned functionality exists before any test code
No verification ran before all functionality was implemented
Changes match the accepted plan
Required outputs exist
Relevant checks have actual results
Unfinished work and blockers are stated accurately

critic.name: Reviewer
critic.instructions: Review in a fresh session; assess the delivered work independently. Inspect changes, requirements and the actual check evidence. List every concrete defect in one pass. Do not approve unfinished requirements.
checks: Every requirement is met
The output satisfies the acceptance checks
Evidence applies to current files
Return APPROVED or REVISE with specific required corrections
